findings.where: The whole tile, first screen most of all: the hero holds the aqueduct drawing, the name and the button, and no part of the tile shows a portrait or a photograph
findings.fault: The look gives no place to Mark's face. It also never shows how a photograph sits on the diazo-blue sheet. The man is a name in capitals under a drawing of the logo.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer weighing a solo advisor wants to see the real person before writing (first-visit trust item 1). Mark asked to be seen and to refresh the images (client value 3, brand sheet §6). The layout round would get no rule for placing his photos or LinkedIn images on this ground.

findings.where: The nav's logo cell (the white arches and the white 'MMM INFRA'), and the palette tile, which leaves out the logo colours
findings.fault: The logo is recoloured to white linework and loses its 'Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services' line. The palette neither includes the logo blue #0070C0 and grey #404040 nor declares them logo-only. In this look, Mark's own mark appears nowhere in its real colours.
findings.who_objects: Mark: the logo stays (client value 7), and a white version he does not hold needs his yes first. Angélique needs to know which logo file goes on this ground.

findings.where: The hero's role line ('LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS', which leaves a dangling bullet at the end of a line on the phone), the nav bar's title-block cells ('DRAWING MMM-GA-001', 'SCALE NTS'), and 'NTS' over the drawing
findings.fault: Drafting jargon sits right next to Mark's name and inside the nav. A visitor has to read and dismiss it, and it pushes 'Infrastructure advisor' into a small line. The title-block cells take the same boxed cells, white caps and link colour as the nav links, so they read as more nav items that do nothing.
findings.who_objects: A bank officer who is not an engineer gets meaningless codes where they look for who Mark is and where to go. Mark wants the page not busy (client value 4), and the codes push it towards a pastiche of a drawing rather than an advisor's page.

findings.where: The hero drawing's amber hatch in the third arch, against the amber 'WRITE TO MARK' button; the palette's 'Sodium amber: daylight in the drawing, and the one action'
findings.fault: One accent has two jobs. The brightest mark at the top of the first screen is decoration in the same amber as the only action, so the eye lands on the drawing before the button. The hatch also contradicts the tile's own texture legend, where hatch means cut earth, not light.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning for how to get in touch: the action colour should mean 'act here' alone. The layout and animation rounds inherit an ambiguous rule for when amber may appear.

findings.where: Hero, the 'WRITE TO MARK' button (a mailto link); no email address appears anywhere on the tile
findings.fault: The only contact route is a mailto link that hides the address. A visitor without a mail client set up clicks it and gets nothing, and the address cannot be copied.
findings.who_objects: Bank and agency staff often use webmail on managed machines. They need the address itself as link text (first-visit trust item 7) to get in touch at all.

findings.where: Article specimen: body text, blockquote and lecture row, set straight on the gridded blueprint ground (desktop-02/03, phone-02)
findings.fault: The article page keeps the full 20 mm and 100 mm grid running behind light body text. The tile shows no calmer reading surface for long prose in Read mode.
findings.who_objects: A reader working through one of Mark's long PPP articles: the grid lines cross every line of text and tire the eye over several screens.

findings.where: Article specimen and type tile: the byline date '18 September 2024' in the sans; the lecture row 'Lecture • 2026-04-23 · PDF' in mono with two different separators; the article heading in mixed case
findings.fault: The specimen breaks the rules the type tile states. The tile says mono for dates and ExtraBold tracked capitals for headings, yet the two dates use different faces and formats, separators mix • and ·, and the article heading is mixed case.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, adding posts, cannot tell from the tile which treatment is the rule. The layout round inherits two answers.

findings.where: Article specimen, the boxed lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' with 'Lecture • 2026-04-23 · PDF'
findings.fault: The whole row has its own box, like a card target, but only the underlined title acts. Clicking 'PDF' or the empty part of the box does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who sees 'PDF' and clicks it to download gets no response.

findings.fault: On the phone the dimension line under the swatches is gone and leaves an empty boxed strip. The poche swatch runs flush to the frame's right edge, while the hatch swatch is inset and a different height.
findings.who_objects: A designer checking the tile on a phone sees a broken-looking specimen, which undercuts the 'measured, exact' character the direction claims.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the 'REPLAY THE CUT' button
findings.fault: A button is drawn as underlined text, which on this page is the mark of a link (as on the lecture title). So the tile never shows what a secondary button looks like.
findings.who_objects: The layout round needs a button rung other than the amber primary. The underline here would make later buttons and links look alike.
